The birth weight and length are printed with a dash between the measurement and the SDS value, which is probably a minus sign lost in printing; the SDS sign was not interpreted and the SDS stays in text_value.

The echocardiography and renal ultrasound sentence carries no time of its own. The echocardiogram is tied to 7 months only through the discussion back-reference; the renal ultrasound suspicion, normal urinary calcium excretion and Bartter suspicion are left untimed and not merged with the Table 1 7-month cells.

Table 1 lists carvedilol and amlodipine at 15 months, while the text says antihypertensive therapy with calcium antagonists and beta-blockers was introduced after the 15-month echocardiogram. The drug names and drug classes were not equated and no start time was assigned.

Table 1 shows None under Therapies at 7, 9 and 12 months; these cells are recorded as absent therapy at those columns. The time at which the diet, spironolactone and amiloride were started is not stated, so no column was assigned to it.

Discussion sentences speculate that hypertension started between 7 and 9 months of age and that the polyuria seemed to worsen during the first year; these are authors hedged interpretations and not recorded as facts.

The discussion says the FENa was normal at presentation at 0.7%. The age of presentation is not stated, so this statement is kept as its own fact and not merged with the 9-month Table 1 value on the matching number.
Values printed inside the growth chart and pedigree figures are pixel content and were not turned into facts; the weight and height SDS values in the text were kept as text facts.
The source gives no age at which apparent mineralocorticoid excess syndrome was diagnosed or treatment began, only the order of the work-up and treatment and the growth velocity at diagnosis.
Table 1 label for the first row header reads FE and Table 1 reports no specimen for the laboratory rows; no specimen was assigned.
The urinary THF + 5α-THF to THE ratio is given as 20 in the case text, while the discussion says ratio values over 20 were seen in this patient; the comparator differs between the two statements.

At 36 months Table 1 prints Normal for cardiac ultrasound while the text says the echocardiogram showed regression of the ventricular hypertrophy; both describe the 36-month examination with different wording and are kept as separate statements.
The 30-month sentence states the urine osmolality time; the following clauses on growth velocity (+0.86 SDS) and weight below −3 SD may share that time but do not state it, so they are left untimed.
The clause "not confirmed by genetic testing" follows the Bartter syndrome suspicion; it is unclear whether genetic testing for Bartter syndrome was performed, so no test fact was added.

The daily blood pressure readings over the four-day hospital stay are placed in the 9-month admission because the discussion says blood pressure readings were not taken until she was nine months old; the stay length is not otherwise dated.
